author: arceuskyske
quote:
The game is undoubtedly a graphical milestone in the video game industry. Wherever you look on the map, you can see where the investment went.

That being said, the game brings absolutely nothing new to the table, with extremely simplistic gameplay mechanics.

I would even consider the gunplay a downgrade compared to Red Dead Redemption 2. Any weapon larger than a pistol is something I simply pick up off the ground during missions.

The life simulation mechanics are cool at first, but they're shallow and repetitive. At some point, I simply got tired of doing them. They're impressive initially, but after dozens of hours, they become tedious and add absolutely nothing meaningful to the experience.

Committing crimes, even something as simple as stealing a car, is incredibly frustrating because the police remember your physical appearance. There were several occasions when I couldn't go somewhere because I was wanted, but I also couldn't buy new clothes because there were no stores available. The game doesn't have instant fast travel (you can call a taxi, though), so whenever I want to escape the police or get back home quickly, I simply quit and reload the game 

The game runs at 30 FPS, and yes, it does suffer from frame drops, especially in heavily forested areas when driving through them.

Another thing that bothers me about the game is the gradual darkening at the edges of the screen. There is no option to disable it.

Finally, what breaks my immersion the most in a game that presents itself as cinematic and somewhat realistic is having obnoxious characters and a story that feels like something straight out of a cheesy American teen movie. First of all, GTA IV isn't nearly this silly (maybe that's why it wasn't as successful?). This makes it incredibly difficult for me to connect with the missions, especially when both protagonists are complete idiots who are responsible for the situations I'm referring to. Those who have played the game know exactly what I mean.

It's perfectly legitimate for people not to enjoy a game like GTA (I personally enjoy Red Dead much more). The magic and impact of a massive game like GTA might last for the first 10 hours or so. After that, if you actually care about how the narrative unfolds, you start noticing how simplistic and shallow its world, story, narrative, characters, and motivations really are.

Some franchises don't necessarily need to be groundbreaking, but for a game of this scale, with this level of investment, these aspects could have been explored with much greater depth.
